questions.stem: A 65-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset severe headache, vomiting, and confusion. Neurological examination reveals signs of meningeal irritation, and the patient's Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score is 13. A non-contrast CT scan of the brain is performed as the initial imaging investigation. CT Findings: The non-contrast CT scan of the brain reveals an asymmetric, hyperdense lesion in the left frontal lobe. The Hounsfield unit (HU) value of the lesion is measured to be +65.
